# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (first)
- Strategy tried: attacked ONE dominant cross-cluster root cause (pandas whole-sheet round-trip
  corrupting the graded workbook) plus stacked additive structure (mandatory inspect/verify,
  type contract, one-code-block). RESULT pending — cannot cite LEDGER yet.
- Diagnosis lever that paid off: reading the SCORER feedback strings literally ("written past
  where the answer ends", "datetime where str expected", "UNCHANGED byte-identical") mapped
  almost 1:1 onto pandas `to_excel` side-effects — the method was the root cause behind
  several superficially different clusters. Prefer method-level fixes over per-task patches here.
- Key guardrail from memory: recalc is grading-side only; in-sandbox verify uses data_only w/o
  recalc, so "write live formulas" is a trap that fights the verification step. Kept literals +
  compute-in-code. Do NOT re-open the formula question without re-reading libreoffice-recalc-active.
- What to try next: if the method fix lands, remaining zeros are likely genuine REASONING-hard
  tasks (SUMIFS date-window 47766, INDEX/MATCH merged-cell 56915) — switch lever to a small
  worked example of that exact idiom rather than more general prose. If rejected on turn budget,
  relax mandatory-INSPECT to conditional.

## cand_0002 (search-process notes; RESULT pending)
- Parallel trace-reading worked well: 3 background subagents (one per trajectory group, incl. all flaky trials) returned concrete per-task root causes in ~2 min, freeing me to design edits. The convergent finding across all 9 tasks — "the prompt LISTS inspect/verify but the weak reader never EXECUTES them" — is only visible by reading traces, not the scorer summary. Keep the fan-out-to-diagnose pattern.
- Meta-lesson confirmed by the traces: cand_0001 added the steps as prose and they were skipped. The right response to a listed-but-skipped step is STRUCTURE (turn-role assignment: "TURN 1 must print and must NOT save"), not another emphatic sentence. Diagnose whether a step is skipped for lack of knowledge (→ prose) or lack of enforcement (→ structure) before choosing the lever.
- Discovered a self-inflicted trap: the parent prompt's own "verification turn re-opens output_path" wording caused a flaky 0 (168-17) because the final graded block is replayed on fresh copies with no output file. Lesson: when the scorer REPLAYS the final artifact, every instruction about the "last step" must keep that artifact self-contained. Audit prompts for last-step wording whenever grading = replay.
- If cand_0002 is rejected, the suspect is the one UNBOUNDED edit (procedure rewrite E1); the additive knowledge/contract edits (E2/E3/E4) are the safe core to retain.

<!-- cap-evolve:meta-insights-append-below -->

## cand_0003 (last iteration of run)
- Strategy: fan-out-to-diagnose (4 subagents) THEN verify every computable fix against the ground-truth
  answer xlsx before shipping. This closed the loop the earlier iterations lacked — I could PROVE the
  recipe reproduces gold on all 3 variants for 49945/43213/52532 rather than hoping. Prefer this: on
  SpreadsheetBench the gold files are on disk, so a prompt fix for a compute task is verifiable, not a guess.
- Lever switch: cand_0001 (prose method) accepted; cand_0002 (more prose + rigid turn-role rewrite) rejected
  with zero measurable movement despite a correct diagnosis. Conclusion: for a weak reader, adding/rewording
  PROSE about a step it skips has diminishing returns. Switched to a single copyable WORKED EXAMPLE that
  encodes the whole correct idiom — the highest-density lever for a model that pattern-matches better than
  it follows instructions.
- Noise reality: n=10 tasks × 3 trials gives 2·SE≈0.17, so only ~2 fully-fixed tasks clear the bar. Small
  additive polish cannot win here; each iteration must land a genuine multi-task fix. Don't ship timid
  batches against this gate.
- What to try next run (if reopened): (1) a second worked example for the merged-cell/cross-sheet key-lookup
  shape (56915, 188-39); (2) if cand_0003 shows no movement, suspect the model ceiling and stop tuning prose —
  the traces show the agent sometimes emits think-only rounds with no code at all, which no prompt reliably
  fixes on an 8B model.
